subject: Escalation: Meridian Health — GPU runway & prioritization request
messages:
From: Alicia Ramos <aramos@meridianhealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Capacity concern ahead of pilot ramp

Connor —

Quick note: our engineering lead saw a projected batch of multi-GPU workloads that will start hitting the pilot next week. The MPA forecast attached shows peak sustained inference concurrency that looks higher than the committed baseline in our dedicated tranche. We were hoping you could confirm: is there headroom for a short-term surge (48–72 hours) without impacting other customers? Procurement is also asking whether we should accelerate the signature to lock dedicated capacity.

We need to understand the practical runway and any restrictions (model variants, quantization differences) so we can decide whether to delay the ramp or proceed with a staged rollout.

Appreciate any quick clarity — we plan a cross-functional call tomorrow at 10am ET.

Thanks,
Alicia Ramos
Senior ML Platform Manager
Meridian Health

Attachment: meridian-mpa-usage-forecast.xlsx (spreadsheet, 34KB)
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Ramos <aramos@meridianhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2027 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Capacity concern ahead of pilot ramp

Alicia —

Thanks for the heads up and for the forecast. Quick summary from our side after a first pass:

- Baseline committed tranche covers the steady-state load described in the contract.
- Short bursts of the magnitude in your forecast will likely exceed the tranche peak by ~25–40% for small windows.
- We have three immediate mitigation levers:
  1) Short-term burst from pool spare capacity (72h max) — impacts are isolated but not unlimited.
  2) Route some non-critical traffic to a quantized-low-precision model variant to reduce per-inference GPU time.
  3) Staged rollout: ramp to 50% pilot then observe a 24–48h window before full ramp.

I can join the cross-functional call tomorrow. If you want a firm commitment today, we can offer a 72-hour burst approval conditioned on: (a) a temporary reduction in throughput for background jobs, and (b) acceptance of a pro-rated overage invoice for burst consumption. Ben and Marcus are cc'd here to review commercial and capacity consequences.

Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
connor@redwood.com

References: Redwood proposed SLA redlines attached.
Attachment: redwood-proposed-sla-redlines.pdf (PDF, 120KB)
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2027 11:27:00 -0800
Subject: INTERNAL: Meridian surge request — need prioritization guidance

Team —

Alicia just sent over a use forecast (attached) showing a ramp that would overshoot their committed tranche for 48–72h. They want a short-term surge allowance so the pilot can start on time. Key constraints and choices: 

Context:
- Meridian is a high-probability expansion in Q1 if pilot performance holds.
- Committed tranche is moderate; the forecast is concentrated and time-bound.

Options (tradeoffs):
1) Grant a 72h burst from pooled spare capacity now. Pros: keeps pilot schedule, strengthens relationship. Cons: consumes spare that other trials may need.
2) Fast-fail route non-critical traffic to a lower-cost quantized model variant (engineering switch) and approve partial burst. Pros: preserves more pool for others; requires dev work from their side.
3) Decline burst; ask Meridian to stagger the ramp. Pros: protects pool equity; Cons: risks delaying pilot and losing momentum.

Questions for Ops/Product: what is current spare capacity across the affected region for the coming weekend? If we have less than 40% spare across tranches, option 1 is risky. Marcus, can you surface a short capacity snapshot? Monica, we need your read on whether Product is comfortable with canarying quantized variants for this account (and the potential QoE hit). Ben, what commercial levers are you willing to offer to secure cooperation (temporary credits, capped overage rates)?

Let's aim to lock a decision in the next 3 hours so I can give Alicia a definitive answer before their procurement call.

Connor
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

> Attachment referenced: meridian-mpa-usage-forecast.xlsx
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Ramos <aramos@meridianhealth.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2027 13:42:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Capacity concern ahead of pilot ramp — temporary runway approved

Alicia —

Appreciate the forecast and the timeline. After a quick ops check with Marcus and a product caveat from Monica, we can approve a controlled 72-hour surge for Meridian with the following conditions:

1) Surge window: Nov 24 00:00 UTC through Nov 27 00:00 UTC (72 hours).
2) Capacity protection: we will provision a temporary elevated tranche equivalent to +30% of your baseline. This will be allocated from pooled spare capacity; we need to limit any single-account additional burst to that amount.
3) Quality mitigation: we recommend routing non-core background inference to the quantized model variant for the surge window. Product (Monica) confirms this is supported but may cause small accuracy deltas — please validate on a staging prompt set first.
4) Commercials: overage for the additional capacity will be invoiced at a capped rate (see attached redline). As a goodwill gesture, we will apply a one-time credit equivalent to the first 8 hours of surge.

Action items for Meridian (please confirm by EOD Nov 22):
- Confirm acceptance of the proposed surge window and the quantized fallback approach.
- Share the final list of background/non-critical traffic to be routed to the quantized model (so we can update routing).

I'll schedule a short follow-up with Marcus and Connor to confirm routing and capacity reservations. If you accept, we'll issue a formal addendum to lock the tranche and the capped overage.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Head of Sales — Enterprise, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-proposed-sla-redlines.pdf (PDF, 120KB); meridian-mpa-usage-forecast.xlsx (spreadsheet, 34KB)
